purpose: Bind judicial propositions to specific judgments and prevent broad conclusions from case summaries.

cases.case: Reidy v The Governor and Company of Bank of Ireland [2023] IECA 212

propositions.statement: Section 31 gives registered entries the statutory conclusive effect specified by the Act, subject to its exceptions and rectification framework.

cases.case: Planetwhite Ltd v Hogan & Anor [2025] IEHC 378

propositions.statement: A registered owner's title under s.31 can be relied upon in possession proceedings, but the register is not automatically conclusive evidence of every term of the underlying transfer or assignment.
Adverse possession/title by possession requires analysis of the claimant's actual possession and the applicable limitation law rather than simply relying on the passage of time.

cases.case: O'Flaherty & Ors v Permanent TSB Public Ltd Company & Ors [2026] IEHC 74

propositions.statement: A dispute concerning the correctness of a Land Registry map and the extent of registered folios may require factual and legal analysis beyond simply identifying the folio/map.

judicial_rule: Every public case-law proposition must retain its case, court, date, issue and factual scope.
remaining: Full judgment audit and additional primary authorities for possessory title and boundaries.
